trickyParts: The architect's literal remedy named one constant root; session_copy has three callers with three roots, which the reviewer caught before the fix was written. The shape that serves all three is an area keyword whose root the function resolves — which also makes an unknown area a refusal rather than a new directory.

Anchoring alone would have left an agent-chosen component with the refusals as its only fence. Taking the component away as well puts them in the right order: the harness names the directory, and the refusals are what catches a mistake in that naming.
A missing pod name in the claim's locator would have become the string `null` through jq and named a directory; `// ""` plus a non-empty test is why it cannot.

discoveredComplexity: A guard measured against a value its caller chose is honest about the wrong thing. Every refusal in session_copy was correct and every one of them was measured against a destination the caller supplied, so relocating the destination defeated all of them at once without breaking any.

Each fix in this class was invisible from inside the one before it: the key-as-path fix reasoned about names, the name-collision fix reasoned about names against directories, and neither could see a hole one level up in the path. The sweep that found each was a search for the class, not for the instance.

Defence in depth has an order. A harness-chosen component with refusals behind it is stronger than an agent-chosen component with refusals in front of it, even though both refuse the same inputs today.
